chunks: Al-‘ākif (the dweller) is he who resides there, and al-bādī (the stranger) is he who comes to perform ḥajj to it from outside the people of Mecca.

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: The people of [Mecca]; referring to the local residents.
key_terms.الْبَادِي: The stranger; one who travels from outside to visit or perform pilgrimage.
key_terms.الْعَاكِفُ: The dweller; one who resides permanently in a place, specifically Mecca.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between al-‘ākif and al-bādī in Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) provides precise lexical definitions to clarify the legal status of residents versus pilgrims, a distinction crucial for the administration of Mecca's sanctity and tax obligations. This clarification reflects the practical governance challenges faced by the governor during the early Islamic period, ensuring that ritual purity and civic duties were correctly applied to each group.
